# Phase 1: Visual Shell - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-02-28
**Status:** Ready for planning

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Isometric office visual shell — landing page, Three.js 3D office view with 16 desks, side drawer with agent/swarm cards, and drag-and-drop agent employment. No AI, no backend. All state is mock data. This phase locks in the rendering approach, visual identity, and interaction patterns that every subsequent phase builds on.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Office 3D Scene & Camera
- Limited orbit camera — user can rotate within ~30-45° range and zoom in/out, constrained so the office always reads well from any allowed angle
- Bright daylight lighting — clean, optimistic natural light through glass walls. Canary Wharf skyline visible and crisp. Premium modern office at 10am feel
- Medium detail environment — recognizable office furniture with texture work: glass walls have reflections, monitors glow, plants and coffee cups as props. Enough to feel alive without being heavy
- Department cluster desk layout — 4 clusters of 4 desks (one per department: Product, Marketing, Creative, Technology). Visual grouping makes the org chart tangible. CPO desk at a prominent position near center/front

### Landing Page & Overall Aesthetic
- Playful-professional visual tone — clean and modern with personality (Notion meets a game lobby). Not boring corporate, not cartoonish. The Minecraft-style agents hint at the playful nature
- 3D rendered preview of the actual office scene as the landing page backdrop — teases what you're about to enter, connects the two experiences seamlessly
- Dark mode default — makes the 3D office scene pop as a hero element. Modern tool energy
- Recent projects displayed as cards with previews — company name, small 3D office thumbnail/icon, last accessed time, active agent count. Visual, scannable, inviting to click

### Character Art & Animation
- Soft blocky style — blocky proportions (big heads, small bodies) with slightly rounded edges and more color detail. Think Crossy Road or Monument Valley characters. Reads as "blocky" but more expressive than pure Minecraft voxel
- Color-coded by department — each department gets a color family (e.g., Product=blue, Marketing=green, Creative=purple, Technology=orange). Characters within a department have unique outfits/accessories but share the color family
- Snappy keyframe animations — quick distinct poses that pop between states. Idle has subtle bob, working has typing motion, talking has head nods and gestures. Game-like feel, immediately readable across 16 characters
- Procedurally generated from code — base character built in Three.js geometry (boxes/cylinders), swap colors/accessories/hair programmatically. Fast iteration, consistent style, no external 3D assets needed

### Drag-Drop & Employment Flow
- Miniature 3D character as drag ghost — small rendered version of the agent's blocky character follows cursor during drag. Bridges the 2D drawer card to the 3D office world
- Subtle glow + pulse drop targets — empty desks get soft green glow and gentle pulse during drag. Hovered desk gets brighter highlight. Guides without being distracting
- Joining animation + toast on successful drop — character materializes at desk with joining animation (walking/popping in with particles), nameplate fades in, status dot lights green. Plus a toast: "Sarah Chen employed as Product Manager"
- Rapid cascade swarm deployment — agents join desks in quick succession with ~200ms delay between each. Managers first, then specialists. Team assembling fast. ~3 seconds for a full swarm

### Claude's Discretion
- Exact orbit camera constraints (precise angle limits)
- Floor material and window view detail level
- Specific department color hex values
- Typography and spacing system
- "Establish New Office" folder picker flow UX details
- Side drawer toggle button placement and animation
- Empty state illustration style ("No offices yet")
- Top nav bar layout specifics
- Loading states and transitions
- Agent card layout details in the drawer

</decisions>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- "Work from bed era" — the product tagline hints at playful irreverence while being a legit productivity tool
- Office should feel like a premium modern glass office on a high floor — Canary Wharf energy
- Characters should feel like Crossy Road / Monument Valley — recognizably blocky but with personality
- Landing page → office transition should feel seamless (3D preview backdrop connects to the actual 3D office)
- Swarm deployment should feel like a team assembling for a mission — rapid, purposeful, exciting

</specifics>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets
- None — greenfield project. Empty frontend/ directory, no existing code

### Established Patterns
- None yet — Phase 1 establishes all patterns (React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind 4, Zustand, Three.js, dnd-kit)

### Integration Points
- ~/.openoffice/projects.json — project registry persisted to user's home directory
- office_config.json — per-project configuration file in project folder
- outputs/ subdirectories — created during "Establish New Office" flow

</code_context>

<deferred>
## Deferred Ideas

None — discussion stayed within phase scope

</deferred>

same dnd-kit drag mechanism | | DRAW-10 | Empty desks highlight as valid drop targets during drag; occupied desks stay neutral | Zustand isDragging flag → desk mesh emissive color via useFrame | --- ## Summary Phase 1 is a pure frontend visual phase — no backend, no AI, no WebSocket. The entire stack runs in the browser. The primary technical challenge is integrating dnd-kit (DOM-based drag-and-drop) with a Three.js r3f scene (WebGL canvas), because the drag source lives in the DOM (side drawer) while drop targets live inside the canvas (3D desk meshes). This cross-boundary drag pattern requires a specific architecture: dnd-kit handles the drag lifecycle and provides the DragOverlay, while Zustand propagates isDragging state into the r3f scene so desk meshes can react visually. Drop detection uses r3f pointer events (onPointerUp on desk meshes) rather than dnd-kit's drop mechanism. The second challenge is procedural character generation using Three.js BoxGeometry. Characters are built entirely in code — no GLTF files, no texture atlases. This is the right decision for iteration speed and style consistency, but requires a structured character factory pattern (groups of BoxGeometry meshes parented together). Animation runs via useFrame with direct mesh mutation (not React state), which is the r3f performance best practice. The third challenge is the "miniature 3D character drag ghost" — rendering a small Three.js scene inside dnd-kit's DragOverlay. This is achievable by placing a second r3f Canvas inside the DragOverlay, but it adds non-trivial complexity (two WebGL contexts, performance cost). Research flags this as LOW confidence — the planner should consider a CSS/canvas 2D fallback if the dual-canvas approach proves too heavy. **Primary recommendation:** Use @react-three/fiber v9 + @react-three/drei + Three.js r167+ as the 3D layer, dnd-kit for drag orchestration, Zustand 5 for shared state bridge between DOM and canvas, React Router v7 declarative mode for routing, and Tailwind 4 with the Vite plugin for all DOM UI. The miniature 3D drag ghost should be prototyped early in plan 01-06 to validate feasibility. --- ## Standard Stack ### Core | Library | Version | Purpose | Why Standard | Router │ ├── App.tsx # Route declarations (react-router v7 declarative) │ ├── index.css # @import "tailwindcss" — only this line needed for v4 │ │ │ ├── pages/ │ │ ├── LandingPage.tsx # Landing with │ │ ├── AgentTab.tsx # Agent list with search │ │ │ ├── AgentCard.tsx # Draggable agent card │ │ │ ├── AgentDetail.tsx # Detail overlay │ │ │ └── SwarmTab.tsx # Swarm cards list │ │ │ │ │ └── ui/ │ │ ├── TopNav.tsx # Logo, company name, settings gear │ │ ├── DragGhost.tsx # Miniature 3D character in DragOverlay │ │ └── Toast.tsx # Sonner Toaster placement │ │ │ ├── store/ │ │ ├── index.ts # Root store combining slices │ │ ├── officeSlice.ts # desks[], agents[], office metadata │ │ ├── dragSlice.ts # isDragging, activeAgent, hoveredDeskId │ │ └── projectsSlice.ts # recentProjects[], createProject action │ │ │ ├── data/ │ │ ├── agents.ts # Full roster mock data (16 agents) │ │ └── swarms.ts # 6 pre-built swarm definitions │ │ │ ├── lib/ │ │ ├── projects.ts # ~/.openoffice/projects.json read/write logic │ │ └── geometry.ts # Three.js geometry helpers │ │ │ └── types/ │ └── index.ts # Agent, Desk, Swarm, Project TypeScript types ``` ### Pattern 1: Zustand Slice Pattern for Office + Drag State **What:** Each domain area (office, drag, projects) has its own slice with typed state and actions. Combined in a root store using intersection types. **When to use:** Always — prevents prop drilling between DOM components and r3f components ```typescript // Source: github.com/pmndrs/zustand docs — slices pattern // store/officeSlice.ts import type { StateCreator } from 'zustand' import type { RootStore } from './index' export interface Desk { id: string position: [number, number, number] // Three.js world position agentId: string | null isPermanent: boolean // CPO desk } export interface OfficeSlice { desks: Desk[] employAgent: (deskId: string, agentId: string) => void initializeOffice: () => void } export const createOfficeSlice: StateCreator = (set) => ({ desks: [], employAgent: (deskId, agentId) => set((state) => ({ desks: state.desks.map((d) => d.id === deskId ? { ...d, agentId } : d ), })), initializeOffice: () => set({ desks: generateDesks() }), // 16 desks across 4 clusters }) // store/dragSlice.ts export interface DragSlice { isDragging: boolean activeAgentId: string | null hoveredDeskId: string | null setDragging: (agentId: string | null) => void setHoveredDesk: (deskId: string | null) => void } export const createDragSlice: StateCreator = (set) => ({ isDragging: false, activeAgentId: null, hoveredDeskId: null, setDragging: (agentId) => set({ isDragging: !!agentId, activeAgentId: agentId }), setHoveredDesk: (deskId) => set({ hoveredDeskId: deskId }), }) ``` ### Pattern 2: Drag-to-3D Architecture (the key cross-boundary pattern) **What:** dnd-kit handles DOM-side drag lifecycle. Zustand propagates drag state to Three.js scene. Drop detection uses r3f pointer events, not dnd-kit's native drop zones. **When to use:** Any time you drag from DOM UI onto a WebGL canvas The architecture has three layers: 1. **dnd-kit** — manages drag source (agent card), DragOverlay, cursor sensor, drag start/end events 2. **Zustand** — isDragging + activeAgentId bridge between DOM and canvas 3. **r3f desk mesh** — reads Zustand.isDragging in useFrame to show/hide highlight; onPointerUp fires the employ action ```typescript // components/drawer/AgentCard.tsx — drag SOURCE in DOM import { useDraggable } from '@dnd-kit/core' function AgentCard({ agent }: { agent: Agent }) { const { attributes, listeners, setNodeRef, transform } = useDraggable({ id: agent.id, data: { type: 'agent', agentId: agent.id }, }) const style = transform ? { transform: `translate3d(${transform.x}px, ${transform.y}px, 0)` } : undefined return (
{/* card content */}
) } ``` ```typescript // components/office/Desk.tsx — drop TARGET in canvas import { useStore } from '../../store' function Desk({ desk }: { desk: Desk }) { const isDragging = useStore((s) => s.isDragging) const hoveredDeskId = useStore((s) => s.hoveredDeskId) const setHoveredDesk = useStore((s) => s.setHoveredDesk) const employAgent = useStore((s) => s.employAgent) const activeAgentId = useStore((s) => s.activeAgentId) const meshRef = useRef(null) // Drive emissive highlight directly — never through React state in useFrame useFrame(() => { if (!meshRef.current) return const mat = meshRef.current.material as THREE.MeshStandardMaterial if (!isDragging || desk.agentId) { mat.emissiveIntensity = 0 } else if (hoveredDeskId === desk.id) { mat.emissiveIntensity = 0.8 // bright green highlight } else { mat.emissiveIntensity = 0.3 // soft pulse (handled by CSS animation or sine wave) } }) const handlePointerUp = () => { if (isDragging && !desk.agentId && activeAgentId) { employAgent(desk.id, activeAgentId) } } return ( isDragging && !desk.agentId && setHoveredDesk(desk.id)} onPointerLeave={() => setHoveredDesk(null)} onPointerUp={handlePointerUp} > ) } ``` ```typescript // OfficePage.tsx — DnDContext wraps BOTH the drawer and the office canvas import { DndContext, DragOverlay } from '@dnd-kit/core' import { useStore } from '../store' function OfficePage() { const setDragging = useStore((s) => s.setDragging) const activeAgentId = useStore((s) => s.activeAgentId) return ( setDragging(e.active.data.current?.agentId)} onDragEnd={() => setDragging(null)} > {/* r3f Canvas */} {/* DOM drawer with draggable cards */} {activeAgentId ? : null} ) } ``` ### Pattern 3: Procedural Character Factory **What:** Pure function receives agent definition → returns `THREE.Group` with all body parts as BoxGeometry meshes, parented together. Colors and accessories swapped per department. **When to use:** For all 16 characters — no GLTF assets needed ```typescript // lib/CharacterFactory.ts // Source: threejs.org BoxGeometry docs + minecraft-style-couple pattern import * as THREE from 'three' interface AgentDef { id: string department: 'product' | 'marketing' | 'creative' | 'technology' accessoryType: 'hat' | 'glasses' | 'headphones' | 'none' } const DEPT_COLORS: Record = { product: '#3b82f6', // blue marketing: '#22c55e', // green creative: '#a855f7', // purple technology: '#f97316', // orange } export function buildCharacter(agent: AgentDef): THREE.Group { const group = new THREE.Group() const color = new THREE.Color(DEPT_COLORS[agent.department]) const mat = (c: THREE.Color | string) => new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: c, roughness: 0.6 }) // Head (bigger than body — Crossy Road proportions) const head = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), mat(color)) head.position.y = 0.95 group.add(head) // Body const body = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.4, 0.5, 0.3), mat(color)) body.position.y = 0.55 group.add(body) // Arms (two, positioned symmetrically) for (const side of [-1, 1]) { const arm = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.15, 0.4, 0.15), mat(color)) arm.position.set(side * 0.3, 0.55, 0) group.add(arm) } // Legs for (const side of [-1, 1]) { const leg = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.18, 0.35, 0.18), mat('#1e1e2e')) leg.position.set(side * 0.12, 0.18, 0) group.add(leg) } // Eyes (white + dark pupil boxes on face) const eyeMat = mat('#ffffff') const pupilMat = mat('#111111') for (const side of [-1, 1]) { const eye = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.1, 0.1, 0.05), eyeMat) eye.position.set(side * 0.12, 1.0, 0.26) group.add(eye) const pupil = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.05, 0.06, 0.06), pupilMat) pupil.position.set(side * 0.12, 0.99, 0.29) group.add(pupil) } group.userData = { agentId: agent.id, department: agent.department } return group } ``` ### Pattern 4: useFrame Animation State Machine **What:** Each character tracks its animation state in a ref (not React state). useFrame applies transform deltas based on current state. **When to use:** All character animations — idle bob, typing, head nod, joining pop ```typescript // components/office/AgentCharacter.tsx // Source: r3f docs — basic-animations, direct mutation pattern function AgentCharacter({ agentId }: { agentId: string }) { const groupRef = useRef(null) const animState = useRef<'idle' | 'working' | 'talking' | 'thinking' | 'joining'>('idle') const elapsed = useRef(0) useFrame((_, delta) => { if (!groupRef.current) return elapsed.current += delta switch (animState.current) { case 'idle': // Subtle vertical bob groupRef.current.position.y = Math.sin(elapsed.current * 1.5) * 0.03 break case 'working': // Slight forward lean + hand bob (simulate typing) groupRef.current.rotation.x = Math.sin(elapsed.current * 4) * 0.05 break case 'joining': // Scale in from 0 over 0.4s const t = Math.min(elapsed.current / 0.4, 1) groupRef.current.scale.setScalar(t) break } }) return } ``` ### Pattern 5: Tailwind v4 with Vite — Zero Config **What:** Tailwind v4 requires only the `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin and `@import "tailwindcss"` in CSS. No `tailwind.config.js`, no content paths. **When to use:** All DOM UI styling — drawer, cards, nav bar, toasts, landing page ```typescript // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react-swc' import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()], }) ``` ```css /* src/index.css */ @import "tailwindcss"; /* That's it — no directives, no config paths */ ``` ### Pattern 6: File System Access API for Folder Picker (LAND-05 / LAND-06) **What:** `window.showDirectoryPicker()` returns a `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` to read/write project files. Works natively in Chromium (Chrome, Edge, Electron). Requires user gesture. **When to use:** "Establish a New Office" button click handler ```typescript // lib/projects.ts async function createOffice(): Promise { try { // Triggers native OS folder picker — requires user gesture const dirHandle = await window.showDirectoryPicker({ mode: 'readwrite' }) const projectPath = dirHandle.name // Only name in web; full path needs Electron IPC // Create office_config.json const configHandle = await dirHandle.getFileHandle('office_config.json', { create: true }) const writable = await configHandle.createWritable() await writable.write(JSON.stringify({ version: 1, createdAt: Date.now() }, null, 2)) await writable.close() // Create outputs/ subdirectories for (const dept of ['product', 'marketing', 'creative', 'technology']) { const outputsDir = await dirHandle.getDirectoryHandle('outputs', { create: true }) await outputsDir.getDirectoryHandle(dept, { create: true }) } return dirHandle.name } catch (err) { if ((err as Error).name === 'AbortError') return null // User cancelled throw err } } ``` **Important caveat:** `showDirectoryPicker()` works in Chromium browsers and Electron's renderer process (as a Chromium-based environment). If this project will be a pure web app, this works. If packaging as Tauri, use `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog` instead. `~/.openoffice/projects.json` full path persistence **requires** either Electron IPC (Node.js `fs`) or Tauri's filesystem plugin — the browser File System Access API cannot resolve `~` paths or write outside the selected directory. ### Anti-Patterns to Avoid - **Updating desk state through React re-renders in useFrame:** Never call `setState` or Zustand setters inside `useFrame`. For continuous animations, mutate mesh properties directly. For discrete events (drop complete), dispatch outside useFrame. - **Creating new THREE objects per frame:** Allocate geometries and materials once, reuse them. Creating `new THREE.BoxGeometry()` inside useFrame causes garbage collection pauses. - **Rendering Three.js components outside Canvas:** All r3f hooks (`useFrame`, `useThree`, etc.) must be called inside a `` component. DOM UI (nav, drawer) must live outside Canvas. - **Two DndContext instances:** Wrap the entire page (Canvas + drawer) in a single `DndContext` so drag events from the drawer can resolve drop targets that react to canvas state. - **Using dnd-kit droppable for 3D drop targets:** dnd-kit's `useDroppable` uses DOM elements; 3D meshes don't have DOM presence. Use Zustand + r3f pointer events for drop detection instead. - **Tailwind v4 with postcss/tailwind.config.js:** v4 uses the Vite plugin, not PostCSS config. The old setup (npx tailwindcss init, postcss.config.js) doesn't apply to v4. - **Importing from "react-router-dom":** v7 merged the packages. Import everything from "react-router" only. --- ## Don't Hand-Roll | Problem | Don't Build | Use Instead | Why | |---------|-------------|-------------|-----| | Camera orbit constraints | Custom camera rig | `` from @react-three/drei | Handles damping, polar/azimuth limits, zoom, mobile touch | | Drag-and-drop lifecycle | Custom mouse event tracking | @dnd-kit/core | Handles pointer capture, keyboard accessibility, scroll detection, multi-touch | | HTML labels above 3D objects | CSS `position: absolute` math | `` component from @react-three/drei | Automatically projects 3D position to screen space, handles occlusion | | Environment/ambient lighting | Custom light setup | `` from @react-three/drei | Provides HDRI environment maps, preset options including "city", "sunset" | | Toast notifications | Custom toast component | sonner | Handles stacking, positioning, dismiss, promise toasts | | 3D character animation sequences | Timeline/keyframe library | `useFrame` with direct ref mutation | For simple state-based animations (5 states), useFrame is sufficient; Theatre.js adds complexity not needed here | **Key insight:** The r3f/drei ecosystem covers camera, lighting, HTML labels, and environment out of the box. The biggest custom work is the procedural character factory and the drag-to-3D bridge pattern — both are intentional design decisions with no off-shelf solutions. --- ## Common Pitfalls ### Pitfall 1: Drag-to-Canvas Drop Not Firing **What goes wrong:** `onPointerUp` on the desk mesh never fires during a drag, even when the user releases over the desk. **Why it happens:** dnd-kit captures the pointer (via `setPointerCapture`) when dragging starts. Pointer capture routes all subsequent pointer events to the original drag source element (the agent card), bypassing the canvas entirely. **How to avoid:** Don't rely on `onPointerUp` alone. Instead: (1) use `onDragEnd` in dnd-kit to get final cursor position, (2) use `getBoundingClientRect()` on the canvas to check if the drop point is over the canvas, then (3) use Three.js raycaster manually to find which desk was under the cursor at drop time. **Warning signs:** Drop handler never fires. Works fine when not using dnd-kit (plain pointer events work). Alternative cleaner approach: Use `eventSource` prop on r3f Canvas to listen for pointer events from the root container element, so the raycaster still runs even during dnd-kit captures. ### Pitfall 2: r3f v9 ThreeElements JSX Types **What goes wrong:** TypeScript errors on custom Three.js JSX elements like ``, ``. **Why it happens:** r3f v9 deprecated global JSX namespace; elements now declared via `ThreeElements` interface. **How to avoid:** Add `/// ` to `vite-env.d.ts`, or explicitly import `ThreeElements` in custom element type declarations. **Warning signs:** TypeScript errors saying "Property 'args' does not exist on type..." or "JSX element type has no construct signature". ### Pitfall 3: Tailwind v4 Dark Mode Configuration **What goes wrong:** Dark mode classes (dark:bg-gray-900) don't apply even with `darkMode: 'class'` config. **Why it happens:** Tailwind v4 doesn't use `tailwind.config.js`. Dark mode configuration is done differently in v4 using CSS custom properties and the `@variant dark` directive. **How to avoid:** For v4, use the CSS-first dark mode approach: set `html.dark` class via JavaScript, then use Tailwind v4's dark variant. Check Tailwind v4 docs before assuming v3 config patterns apply. **Warning signs:** Dark mode classes compile but don't apply visually. ### Pitfall 4: Dual r3f Canvas Performance (Drag Ghost) **What goes wrong:** The miniature 3D character drag ghost (rendered as a second r3f Canvas inside DragOverlay) causes frame drops to 30fps when dragging. **Why it happens:** Two active WebGL rendering contexts compete for GPU resources. The DragOverlay canvas triggers its own requestAnimationFrame loop, doubling GPU work during drag. **How to avoid:** (1) Freeze the drag ghost canvas when not dragging — render it once and use it as a static image. (2) Consider rendering the character to a canvas off-screen, then using the canvas as an HTML `` inside DragOverlay (screenshot approach). (3) As a fallback, use a CSS-animated card preview instead of a 3D scene in the overlay. **Warning signs:** Frame rate drops sharply when drag begins and recovers when drag ends. ### Pitfall 5: Zustand Selector Causing Render Loops in r3f **What goes wrong:** Components inside Canvas re-render on every frame because Zustand subscription triggers React re-renders which block r3f's render loop. **Why it happens:** Subscribing to rapidly-changing Zustand state (like `hoveredDeskId`) inside r3f components triggers React reconciliation on each pointer move. **How to avoid:** Use `useStore.subscribe` (non-reactive subscription) inside useFrame to read Zustand state for animation purposes. Only use reactive Zustand selectors for discrete state changes (employ/fire agent). For hover state driving emissive color, store hover in a ref, update it in `onPointerEnter/Leave`, and read it in `useFrame`. **Warning signs:** High CPU usage from React reconciliation visible in React DevTools. Canvas appears to stutter during pointer movement. ### Pitfall 6: File System Access API — No Full Path Access **What goes wrong:** Can't write to `~/.openoffice/projects.json` via `showDirectoryPicker()`. **Why it happens:** The File System Access API sandboxes access to the user-selected directory and its children. It cannot access arbitrary filesystem paths like the user's home directory. **How to avoid:** For pure web builds, store projects.json data in `localStorage` as a fallback. For Electron builds, use Electron IPC to call Node.js `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(os.homedir(), '.openoffice', 'projects.json'), ...)` from the main process. **Warning signs:** `Error: NotAllowedError` when trying to access paths outside the selected folder. ### Pitfall 7: OrbitControls Azimuth Clamping Bug in Three.js **What goes wrong:** When `minAzimuthAngle === maxAzimuthAngle` to lock horizontal rotation, camera snaps or behaves unexpectedly. **Why it happens:** Known Three.js issue #20627: clamping azimuth when min === max has edge cases. **How to avoid:** Use a small epsilon difference (minAzimuthAngle = -0.001, maxAzimuthAngle = 0.001) instead of exact equality. Or use a small range (e.g., -Math.PI/6 to Math.PI/6) for the allowed ~30° horizontal sweep. **Warning signs:** Camera teleports or locks entirely when azimuth limits are too tight. --- ## Code Examples Verified patterns from official sources and verified community patterns: ### Vite Config with Tailwind 4 + SWC ```typescript // vite.config.ts // Source: tailwindcss.com/docs + vitejs.dev import { defineConfig } from 'vite' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react-swc' import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()], }) ``` ### React Router v7 Declarative Mode (2-route SPA) ```typescript // src/App.tsx // Source: reactrouter.com/start/modes — declarative mode import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route } from 'react-router' import LandingPage from './pages/LandingPage' import OfficePage from './pages/OfficePage' export default function App() { return ( } /> } /> ) } ``` ### r3f v9 Canvas with Constrained OrbitControls ```typescript // components/office/CameraRig.tsx // Source: drei.docs.pmnd.rs/controls + threejs.org/docs/OrbitControls import { OrbitControls } from '@react-three/drei' export function CameraRig() { return ( ) } ``` ### Zustand Root Store (Combined Slices) ```typescript // store/index.ts // Source: github.com/pmndrs/zustand — slices pattern, TypeScript import { create } from 'zustand' import { createOfficeSlice, OfficeSlice } from './officeSlice' import { createDragSlice, DragSlice } from './dragSlice' import { createProjectsSlice, ProjectsSlice } from './projectsSlice' export type RootStore = OfficeSlice & DragSlice & ProjectsSlice export const useStore = create()((...args) => ({ ...createOfficeSlice(...args), ...createDragSlice(...args), ...createProjectsSlice(...args), })) ``` ### DndContext + Desk Drop via Raycaster (key pattern) ```typescript // pages/OfficePage.tsx — resolving drop position import { DndContext, DragEndEvent, useSensor, PointerSensor } from '@dnd-kit/core' import { useThree } from '@react-three/fiber' import { useRef } from 'react' import * as THREE from 'three' // In the r3f scene component — raycaster-based drop resolver function DropResolver({ onDrop }: { onDrop: (deskId: string, agentId: string) => void }) { const { camera, scene, gl } = useThree() // Called by parent DndContext onDragEnd // Must use gl.domElement.getBoundingClientRect() to convert client coords to NDC return null } ``` ### Desk Pulse Animation (Tailwind CSS + useFrame hybrid) ```typescript // For DOM-overlaid pulse effect on empty desk highlight: // Use Tailwind 'animate-pulse' on an absolute div positioned over desk using drei // For mesh-level emissive glow, use useFrame: useFrame(({ clock }) => { if (!meshRef.current || !isDragging || desk.agentId) return const mat = meshRef.current.material as THREE.MeshStandardMaterial // Sine wave pulse: 0.2 to 0.5 intensity at 2Hz mat.emissiveIntensity = 0.2 + Math.sin(clock.elapsedTime * Math.PI * 2) * 0.15 mat.emissive.set('#00ff88') }) ``` --- ## State of the Art | Old Approach | Current Approach | When Changed | Impact | |--------------|------------------|--------------|--------| | @react-three/fiber v8 (React 18) | @react-three/fiber v9 (React 19) | 2024 | ThreeElements JSX type changes; must use v9 for React 19 | | react-router-dom | react-router (merged packages) | v7 (2024) | Import from "react-router" only; v7 has 3 modes | | Tailwind config-based setup | @tailwindcss/vite plugin, no config | v4 (Jan 2025) | `tailwind.config.js` no longer needed; `@import "tailwindcss"` in CSS | | MeshProps, Object3DNode r3f types | ThreeElements['mesh'] | r3f v9 | All Three.js JSX types accessed through ThreeElements interface | | create() basic Zustand | Slices pattern with middleware | Zustand 5 (2024) | zustand@5.0.10 (Jan 2026) fully React 19 compatible | | react-beautiful-dnd | @dnd-kit/core | 2022-onward | react-beautiful-dnd unmaintained; dnd-kit is current standard | **Deprecated/outdated:** - **react-beautiful-dnd**: Archived/unmaintained. Use @dnd-kit/core. - **@react-three/fiber v8 with React 19**: Incompatible. Use v9. - **tailwind.config.js for v4**: Not used. Vite plugin replaces PostCSS workflow. - **Global JSX namespace in r3f**: Deprecated. Use `ThreeElements` interface. --- ## Open Questions 1. **Miniature 3D drag ghost feasibility** - What we know: dnd-kit's DragOverlay accepts any React component; a second `` can theoretically live inside it - What's unclear: GPU performance with two active WebGL contexts; whether the second canvas initializes fast enough during drag start; whether the character renders correctly at small scale (48-64px) - Recommendation: Build a prototype in plan 01-06 day 1. Have a CSS fallback ready (card preview with character color and emoji). If dual-canvas approach drops frame rate below 55fps, use the fallback. Consider rendering ghost to an off-screen canvas once and using as `` (screenshot approach). 2. **`~/.openoffice/projects.json` persistence in a pure web app** - What we know: File System Access API cannot access arbitrary paths; it's sandboxed to selected directories - What's unclear: Is this app packaged as Electron/Tauri, or pure web? Not specified in CONTEXT.md - Recommendation: For Phase 1, use `localStorage` as the projects.json store (keys prefixed `openoffice:projects`). If Electron packaging is added later, swap to Electron IPC. The API shape stays identical — swap the persistence layer without changing the Zustand store. 3. **Drop detection with dnd-kit pointer capture** - What we know: dnd-kit's PointerSensor calls `setPointerCapture` on drag start; r3f raycaster is affected by this - What's unclear: Whether the r3f `eventSource` prop allows raycasting to continue working through pointer capture - Recommendation: Test with `eventSource={rootRef}` on Canvas where rootRef is the page root div. If raycasting still fails, fall back to: store the drop zone bounding boxes in DOM, compare final cursor position against desk positions in onDragEnd. --- ## Sources ### Primary (HIGH confidence) - r3f.docs.pmnd.rs/getting-started/installation — r3f v9 + React 19 pairing, Three.js peer dep, install command - r3f.docs.pmnd.rs/tutorials/v9-migration-guide — Breaking changes: ThreeElements, CanvasProps rename, GL prop changes - drei.docs.pmnd.rs/controls/introduction — OrbitControls API, polar/azimuth constraints - github.com/pmndrs/zustand — Slices pattern, TypeScript usage, zustand v5 release date - tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4 — v4 zero-config, Vite plugin, @import syntax change - reactrouter.com/start/modes — v7 declarative mode, package consolidation to "react-router" - developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Window/showDirectoryPicker — File System Access API, Chromium support ### Secondary (MEDIUM confidence) - npmjs.com/package/@react-three/fiber — v9.5.0 current version (published ~2 months before research) - npmjs.com/package/@dnd-kit/react — @dnd-kit/react 0.3.2, DragOverlay confirmed present - npmjs.com/package/zustand — v5.0.10 release date confirmed 2026-01-12 - github.com/pmndrs/drei/discussions/2213 — React 19 + R3F v9 compatibility confirmed in discussion - WebSearch: Tailwind v4 install guide (2025) — confirmed @tailwindcss/vite + @import pattern - WebSearch: dnd-kit DragOverlay architecture — portal-mounted, custom children supported - WebSearch: OrbitControls azimuth constraint properties — minAzimuthAngle/maxAzimuthAngle confirmed - github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/20627 — azimuth clamping bug when min===max confirmed ### Tertiary (LOW confidence) - Miniature 3D character in DragOverlay: No official docs or community examples found for dual r3f Canvas in DragOverlay. Theoretically possible; performance untested. **Flag for early prototype.** - dnd-kit + r3f pointer capture interaction: No official documentation found for this specific combination. Community discussion suggests custom raycaster approach. **Flag for early prototype.** - `showDirectoryPicker` in Electron: MDN confirms Chrome/Edge support; Electron renders in Chromium so should work, but no official Electron docs specifically confirming it. **Likely works; verify in plan 01-02.** --- ## Metadata **Confidence breakdown:** - Standard stack: HIGH — all packages verified via npm and official docs with current versions - Architecture patterns: HIGH for Zustand slices, r3f/drei usage, Tailwind v4, react-router v7; MEDIUM for drag-to-3D pattern (no off-shelf example found, but architecture is sound); LOW for miniature 3D drag ghost (untested pattern) - Pitfalls: HIGH for pointer capture issue (known r3f community problem), Tailwind v4 dark mode, r3f v9 types; MEDIUM for others **Research date:** 2026-02-28 **Valid until:** 2026-03-28 (stable libraries; r3f/drei patch releases unlikely to break patterns)
